system:
You are recording the study profile of a scientific manuscript for study-design planning: what it measured, how, and with which designs and models.
You do not judge the science; you report what the manuscript says, anchored to verbatim text.
Rules:
- `variables`: every concept the study measured or modelled (outcomes, exposures, covariates, stratifiers, offsets/denominators, effect modifiers), with its `role`, and its `operationalization`: how the manuscript measured or derived it (e.g. "postconceptional age = gestational age at birth + chronological age, in weeks"). Name the `concept` in plain domain terms (e.g. "maternal smoking during pregnancy"), not as a dataset column.
- Every variable carries a `quote`: one verbatim span (15-300 characters) copied exactly from the text, character for character, that shows the concept being measured or modelled, and the `page` from the `[page N]` marker it comes from. Do not shorten, paraphrase, or append page markers to the quote; paraphrases are rejected.
- `research_questions`: the questions or aims the text states, one per item.
- `data_sources_used`: the datasets the study analysed, named as written.
- `designs` and `model_classes`: only values from the allowed vocabulary below that describe what this text reports doing.
- Fill every field. An empty list is correct only when this part of the text contains none of that item (for example a references section).
- Report at most 60 variables. If the text contains more (for example a collection of abstracts), keep those most relevant to study design; never enumerate exhaustively.

Allowed study designs:
- cohort: Follow a defined population forward; outcome incidence by exposure.
- case_control: Cases vs sampled controls; exposure odds compared.
- nested_case_control: Case-control sampled from within an enumerated cohort.
- cross_sectional: Exposure and outcome measured at one time.
- population_incidence: Counts of events over a denominator population (rates).
- case_crossover: Each case serves as its own control across time windows.
- ecological: Group-level exposure and outcome.
Allowed model classes:
- logistic_regression: Binary outcome; odds ratios.
- conditional_logistic: Binary outcome with matched sets.
- log_binomial: Binary outcome; risk ratios directly.
- poisson_regression: Counts/rates with offset; assumes mean = variance.
- negative_binomial: Overdispersed counts/rates with offset.
- cox_proportional_hazards: Time-to-event; hazard ratios.
- time_stratified: Any of the above fit separately within time strata (e.g. PCA windows).
- generalized_additive: Smooth nonlinear terms (e.g. risk as a smooth function of age).
- linear_regression: Continuous outcome.

Manuscript "bedsharing_ms_v7", pages 1 to 1. Page boundaries are marked `[page N]`.


[page 1]

Supplementary Material
Editorial note: to be separated into a standalone supplementary file before submission. Numbers trace to AJE/v3 (primary, PCA 36 to 90) and AJE/v4 (sensitivity, PCA 36 to 79).
Supplementary Table 1. PCA window boundary diagnostics
Prespecified PCA window (36-90 weeks) checked against a count-stability criterion of at least 5 cases per week in each of 4 tracked subgroups (bed sharing, non-bed sharing, male, female), and compared against an equivalent symmetric percentage trim. Values trace to the original R1.2/R1.3 boundary verification. Table to be inserted from supp_table3_boundary_diagnostics.xlsx during composite assembly.
Supplementary Table 2. PCA<=79 upper-bound sensitivity comparison
Late-window incidence rate ratios at the primary PCA window (36-90 weeks) versus an upper-bound sensitivity analysis restricting the window to PCA 36-79 weeks. Values trace to AJE/v3 (primary) and AJE/v4 (sensitivity). Table to be inserted from supp_table4_pca79_sensitivity.xlsx during composite assembly.
Supplementary Table 3. Prespecified interaction terms from the windowed negative binomial models
Adjusted incidence rate ratios, 95% confidence intervals, and P values for the bed sharing by maternal smoking and bed sharing by preterm birth product terms in the early and late windowed negative binomial models. Values trace to AJE/v3. Table to be inserted from r1_7_interaction_table.xlsx during composite assembly.
Supplementary Table 4. Sex-stratified windowed incidence rate ratios
Adjusted incidence rate ratios and P values for PCA, bed sharing, maternal smoking, and preterm birth in the early and late windowed negative binomial models, stratified by sex. Values trace to AJE/v3. Table to be inserted from supp_table5_sex_stratified_irr.xlsx during composite assembly.
Supplementary Table 5. Birthweight-stratified windowed incidence rate ratios
Adjusted incidence rate ratios for bed sharing in low-birthweight and non-low-birthweight strata, and for the bed sharing by low-birthweight interaction, in the early and late windowed negative binomial models. Values trace to AJE/v3. Table to be inserted from supp_table6_birthweight_stratified_irr.xlsx during composite assembly.
Supplementary Table 6. Smoking-stratified windowed incidence rate ratios
Adjusted incidence rate ratios for bed sharing in maternal-smoking and non-smoking strata in the early and late windowed negative binomial models, and the share of deaths occurring before one month of age by bed-sharing and smoking status. Values trace to AJE/v3. Table to be inserted from supp_table7_smoking_stratified_irr.xlsx during composite assembly.
Supplementary Table 7. PCA versus chronological-age GAM fit comparison
Deviance, log-likelihood, AIC, model degrees of freedom, and pseudo R-squared for the negative binomial generalized additive model fit separately on the PCA axis and the chronological-age axis. Values trace to AJE/v3. Table to be inserted from e9_fit_comparison_table.xlsx during composite assembly.
Supplementary Figure 1. Observed and fitted incidence by time axis
Observed and GAM-fitted weekly SUID incidence plotted separately on the PCA axis and the chronological-age axis, underlying the deviance comparison in Supplementary Table 7. File: observed_by_axis.png/.tiff (AJE/v3/out_joint/output_data/ncfrp/time_axes/).
